title: DAXDA Next-Gen Polar Paleobiogeography, Marine/Organic Ice Contents & Geomagnetic vs. Tectonic Displacement Map

track.notes: Reached on foot on Polar Plateau
Drifting NW across George V Land toward Adelie Coast
Crossed Antarctic coastline near Dumont d'Urville
Offshore Wilkes Land (~2,860 km from Geographic South Pole), drifting NW at ~10–15 km/yr

physical_displacement_synthesis.1_magnetic_pole_drift: Rapid Outer-Core Dynamo Drift: The South Magnetic Pole has migrated 1404.2 km northwest between 1841 (75.05°S, 154.13°E) and 2025 (64.01°S, 135.88°E) — and flipped completely during the 41,000 yr BP Laschamp Excursion recorded in Vostok/Dome C 10Be ice cores.
physical_displacement_synthesis.2_basal_ice_marine_conveyor: Vertical Glacial Transport (0–100 m): Live saltwater sponges, bivalves, and hypersaline marine brines (McMurdo 'Dirty Ice' & Blood Falls) are not evidence of a sudden ocean wave washing over the continent; they are trapped sub-shelf seafloor organisms and Pliocene fjord waters carried upward by basal adfreezing and surface katabatic wind ablation.
physical_displacement_synthesis.3_gondwana_plate_tectonics_and_greenhous: Horizontal Plate Tectonic Separation (2,400–6,800 km over 34–260 Myr): The subtropical palm pollen (Wilkes Land U1356, 52 Ma), temperate rainforest root systems (Pine Island PS104, 90 Ma), Eocene warm-water marine shells (Seymour Island), and Permian Glossopteris trees (Beardmore Glacier, 260 Ma) map directly to Antarctica's pre-rift Gondwana conjugates — Patagonia, New Zealand (Zealandia), Tasmania/Australia, and South Africa — combined with Cretaceous/Eocene greenhouse periods when polar latitudes were frost-free.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: Swedish Antarctic Expedition (Ship: Antarctic, Otto Nordenskjöld)
mapped_records.site_name: Seymour Island & Snow Hill Island (James Ross Basin)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: Coastal outcrop & periglacial marine terraces (0–200 m ASL)
contents_found: Warm-water Eocene saltwater marine mollusks (bivalves Cucullaea, gastropods)
Giant Eocene penguin bones (Palaeeudyptes) & shark teeth
Subtropical/warm-temperate fossil wood, Araucaria conifers, ferns, and Nothofagus leaves
mapped_records.age_of_material: 66 to 34 Million Years Ago (Late Cretaceous to Eocene)

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Patagonia / Tierra del Fuego & Southern Chile (Magallanes Basin)

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Prior to the opening of the Drake Passage (~34 Ma), the Antarctic Peninsula was physically connected to South America (Patagonia), and warm subtropical ocean gyres reached the Antarctic coast.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: British Antarctic Expedition (Ship: Terra Nova, R.F. Scott & E. Wilson)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: Nunatak coal seam emerging through glacial ice (~2,200 m ASL)
contents_found: 35 lbs of Permian Glossopteris deciduous tree leaf fossils
Bituminous coal seams and fossilized woody peat trunks

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Gondwana Supercontinent — Hunter Valley (Australia) & Karoo Basin (South Africa)
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: ~65°S–70°S during icehouse-to-greenhouse Permian transition inside unified Gondwana

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Continental drift (plate tectonics): East Antarctica was sutured directly to Australia, India, and Southern Africa in the Gondwana supercontinent.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: USASE (Ships: USS Bear & USMS North Star) & Argentine ARA Primero de Mayo (1942)
mapped_records.site_name: Deception Island / Stonington Island / Little America III (Ross Shelf)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: 0 m sea-level caldera to 41 m Ross Shelf boreholes
contents_found: Ross Shelf 7m pit & 41m borehole hexagonal Ice Ih density/temperature profiles (F. Alton Wade)
Deception Island submarine fumarole-melted glacial ice & marine benthic specimens (ARA Primero de Mayo, Feb 1942)
Palmer Peninsula hydrothermal quartz-pyrite-Cu-Au veins & lichen/moss flora (Paul Knowles)
mapped_records.biological_type: Glacial Ice Ih + Hydrothermal Marine-Glacial Interface

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Andean Cordillera Metallogenic & Volcanic Arc (Atacama / Potosí Meridian)

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Structural and volcanic continuity of the Andean Cordilleran arc across the Scotia Arc into the Antarctic Peninsula.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: Discovery Expedition & McMurdo Ice Shelf ('Dirty Ice') Ablation Studies
mapped_records.site_name: McMurdo Ice Shelf & Black Island Debris Bands (McMurdo Sound)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: Found atop the surface of the floating ice shelf (migrated upward from 40–100 m basal depth)
contents_found: Intact saltwater marine glass sponges (Hexactinellida), bryozoans, and polychaete worm tubes
Articulated marine bivalve shells (Adamussium colbecki) and benthic foraminifera
Mirabilite (sodium sulfate) saltwater brine crystals and marine mud
mapped_records.biological_type: Saltwater Marine Benthic Invertebrates on Ice Surface

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Ross Sea Continental Shelf Seafloor (Basal Adfreeze Zone)
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: In-situ Southern Ocean sub-shelf seafloor lifted vertically through the ice column

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Basal adfreezing & surface ablation conveyor: Seawater freezes onto the bottom of the ice shelf, trapping live seafloor sponges, shells, and saltwater sediment; katabatic wind ablation removes top snow, bringing the basal marine floor organisms all the way to the top surface of the ice.

mapped_records.era_or_year: 1911–2023 (Griffith Taylor 1911; Mikucki et al. 2009 / Badger Explorer)
mapped_records.ship_or_project: Terra Nova Discovery / USAP Subglacial Brine & Ice-Penetrating Radar
mapped_records.site_name: Blood Falls, Taylor Glacier (McMurdo Dry Valleys)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: Subglacial hypersaline marine reservoir ~400 m beneath Taylor Glacier
contents_found: Ancient trapped saltwater marine brine (salinity ~2.5x normal ocean water, rich in ferrous iron Fe2+)
Active extremophile marine microbial ecosystem (Desulfocapsa, Thiomicrospira) metabolizing sulfate & iron without oxygen or light
mapped_records.age_of_material: 1.5 to 5 Million Years Ago (Pliocene marine fjord isolation)

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Ancient Pliocene Ross Sea Fjord Network (Open-water Taylor Fjord)
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: 77.7°S during Pliocene warm optimum when Dry Valleys were open saltwater marine fjords

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: When the Taylor Valley marine fjord uplifted and Taylor Glacier advanced over it ~1.5–5 Ma, relic ocean water was sealed beneath 400 m of glacial ice and cryoconcentrated into hypersaline brine.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: ANDRILL (Antarctic Geological Drilling Project, MIS Core AND-1B)
mapped_records.site_name: Ross Ice Shelf Drill Site (McMurdo Sound)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: 1,285 m sub-ice core drilled through 85 m thick floating ice shelf and 800 m seawater
contents_found: 85+ cycles of greenish saltwater marine diatomite ooze (open-ocean photosynthetic algae)
Warm-water silicoflagellates and marine organic biomarkers indicating +3°C to +5°C warmer ocean waters

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Subantarctic Open Ocean / Southern New Zealand Marine Front
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: 77.9°S during periodic collapses of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet into an open marine sea

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Orbital obliquity & CO2-driven oscillations (~40,000-year cycles) repeatedly melted the Ross Ice Shelf, replacing 1,000 m of glacial ice with open, sunlit saltwater diatom seas.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: Integrated Ocean Drilling Program (Ship: JOIDES Resolution, Expedition 318, Site U1356)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: 1,000 m below seafloor off the Wilkes Land ice sheet margin
contents_found: Cold-intolerant tropical/subtropical palm tree pollen (Arecipites)
Baobab-relative pollen (Bombacacidites), Proteaceae, and Macadamia-family flora
Soil bacterial branched GDGT organic lipid thermometers showing winter temperatures >10°C (frost-free) and summer ~25°C
mapped_records.biological_type: Subtropical / Frost-Free Coastal Rainforest Organic Pollen & Lipids
mapped_records.age_of_material: 52 to 53 Million Years Ago (Early Eocene Climatic Optimum)

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Tasmania / Southern Australia & North Island New Zealand Subtropical Forests
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: ~65°S–67°S along the rifting Australia-Antarctica coastal seaway

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: High Eocene atmospheric CO2 (~1,000+ ppm) plus warm poleward ocean currents maintained a frost-free, subtropical palm coast along East Antarctica even at ~65°S polar latitude.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: RV Polarstern Expedition PS104 (MeBo70 Seafloor Drill Core PS104_20-2)
mapped_records.site_name: Pine Island & Thwaites Glacier Trough (Amundsen Sea, West Antarctica)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: 27–30 m sub-seafloor core beneath retreating West Antarctic glacier margin
contents_found: Intact CT-scanned 3D root network in fine-grained organic peat soil
62+ terrestrial plant pollen & spore taxa including conifers (Podocarpaceae), tree ferns (Cyatheaceae), and flowering angiosperms
Freshwater cyanobacterial organic mat biomarkers
mapped_records.biological_type: Swampy Temperate Rainforest Soil, Roots & Spores

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: South Island New Zealand (Fiordland / Westland Temperate Rainforest, originally joined to Marie Byrd Land)
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: ~82°S (only ~900 km from the Cretaceous South Pole!)

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Before the Zealandia (New Zealand) microcontinent rifted away from West Antarctica (~85 Ma), Marie Byrd Land and New Zealand formed a single contiguous temperate rainforest landmass.

mapped_records.ship_or_project: Vostok & EPICA Dome C Deep Ice Cores (3,769 m & 3,270 m depth)
mapped_records.site_name: Vostok Station / Lake Vostok & Dome C (East Antarctic Plateau)
mapped_records.sample_depth_or_elevation: 0 to 3,769 m pure glacial Ice Ih core (3,539–3,769 m Lake Vostok accretion ice)
contents_found: Cosmogenic Beryllium-10 (10Be) twofold spike at ~41,000 yr BP (Laschamp Geomagnetic Excursion) & ~780,000 yr BP (Brunhes-Matuyama Reversal)
Accretion ice above Lake Vostok (>3,539 m) containing thermophilic/chemolithotrophic bacterial DNA (Hydrogenophilus) and dissolved organic carbon
800,000 years of trapped atmospheric CO2, CH4, volcanic sulfate, and marine sea-salt (Na+) aerosols
mapped_records.biological_type: Subglacial Accretion Ice Microbiome + Cosmogenic Geomagnetic Record
mapped_records.age_of_material: 0 to 800,000 Years BP (Ice Core); >15 Million Years isolation (Lake Vostok)

mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.region: Global Geomagnetic Dipole Reversal Axis (Magnetic Pole migrated across Equator during Laschamp 41 ka)
mapped_earth_origin_or_conjugate.paleolatitude_at_deposition: East Antarctic Craton remained stationary at ~78°S while the Magnetic Pole flipped globally

mapped_records.scientific_mechanism: Crucial distinction between Magnetic Pole Shift and Crustal Displacement: The 10Be ice-core record proves that Earth's magnetic dipole collapsed to <6% strength and wandered across the equator 41,000 years ago (Laschamp Excursion) WITHOUT any physical slippage of the continental crust.
